name: Non-syndromic urogenital tract malformation of male and female

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging criteria for non-syndromic urogenital malformations

criteria.description: Presence of congenital structural anomalies of the urogenital tract confirmed by imaging or surgical findings
No associated syndromic features or systemic malformations on clinical and genetic evaluation
Normal chromosomal analysis excluding known syndromic chromosomal abnormalities
Positive family history of isolated urogenital malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital urogenital tract malformation confirmed by imaging or surgery with exclusion of syndromic features and chromosomal abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, imaging, and genetic assessments.

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly presents as urinary retention or weak stream in males
Typically identified in adolescent females with primary amenorrhea
Abnormal ventral urethral opening in males

common.notes: Secondary to urinary stasis or obstruction
Mild to moderate genital malformations without syndromic features

occasional.notes: Rare severe malformation with exposed bladder mucosa

rare.notes: Unilateral or bilateral absence of kidney
Rare complex malformation involving urogenital and anorectal tracts
Common channel for urinary and genital tracts
searchTerms: abnormal urinary and genital tract connection

laboratory: Urinalysis showing recurrent infections or hematuria
imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating structural anomalies of kidneys, ureters, bladder, or genital tract
Voiding cystourethrogram showing urethral obstruction or reflux
MRI pelvis for detailed soft tissue anatomy
genetic: Possible familial clustering without syndromic features
other: Surgical findings confirming isolated urogenital malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic anomalies or dysmorphic features
Associated vertebral and lower limb anomalies

redFlags: Severe urinary obstruction causing renal impairment
Recurrent urinary tract infections with fever
references: Orphanet: Non-syndromic urogenital tract malformation of male and female, ORPHA:182124
Jones KL. Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation. 7th Edition. 2013.
